candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — radiation-treatment skin care and comfort
candidate.educational_objective: Teach gentle, team-directed skin care during radiation therapy and avoidance of direct heating pads or ice packs on the treatment field.

options.A: I will use only skin products recommended by my radiation team and avoid heating pads or ice packs on the treatment area.
options.B: I will place an ice pack directly on the treatment area whenever the skin feels warm or irritated.
options.C: I can use any fragranced lotion or alcohol-based product as long as the skin has not started to peel.
options.D: I should scrub the treatment area firmly each day to remove dry or flaking skin before my radiation session.

candidate.rationale: NCI guidance advises clients receiving radiation therapy to use only skin products recommended by the healthcare team and to use gentle skin care because the treated skin may become dry, tender, irritated, or peel. NCI specifically advises not to use heating pads or ice packs on the radiation treatment area. Products containing alcohol or fragrance may irritate or dry the skin, and vigorous scrubbing can further injure sensitive tissue.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NCI recommends team-directed gentle skin care during radiation therapy, use of recommended products, avoidance of heating pads and ice packs on the treatment area, and avoidance of irritating products such as those containing alcohol or fragrance.
